title: 339 comment sentences over 40 words across 193 of 329 cell files (criterion C5)
claim: Counted within prose paragraphs only (list items, RESULT lines and indentation steps split apart), 339 sentences in the D5 units of the seat's 329 files exceed the 40-word ceiling D5-criteria.md C5 sets, in 193 files; the hooks alone carry examples of 41-53 words (pre-edit.sh lines 4-7, 34-40, 211-216).
mechanism: Comments accrete narrative history (who measured, which PR) inside a single sentence joined by dashes and semicolons; no lint bounds sentence length.

evidence.machine: box B12, x86_64 Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz, 4 vCPU, Python 3.14.7, node v22.23.4
evidence.contention_note: shared box during fan-out; a count, contention-immune
evidence.tolerance: ±5 % (the textual splitter: an abbreviation can split early, a list without a marker can merge)

instrumented_symbol: tools/audit/text_ledger.py:units_of and :sentences over every D5 unit of the seat's cells

perturbation.change: --rewrite ', so =. So ' (splitting each such sentence at its ', so' clause, in memory)

metric_definition: long_sentences: sentences (text_ledger.sentences within a prose paragraph of a D5 unit) longer than 40 whitespace words
phenomenon_property: No sentence in a comment or docstring of the cells exceeds 40 words.
proposed_fix_scope: split or cut the flagged sentences, history clauses first (C4); a sentence-length lint over D5 units would hold it
